name: Prime Tower
features: 126 m green-glass office tower whose irregular octagonal plan steps out in two places as it rises.
note: Tallest building in Switzerland 2011-2015, per Wikipedia.

name: Kirchner Museum Davos
features: Four glass-clad gallery cubes linked by a low glazed hall; daylight enters the rooms from above.
note: Gigon/Guyer's breakthrough work (1989-1992 per Wikipedia's project list). The 'four cubes' and top-light description is from general knowledge of the building and the photos; check before publishing.

name: Toni-Areal
features: Former yoghurt factory turned into an art university: a vertical campus with a ramp running through it.
note: No English Wikipedia article. Architect EM2N from the Commons file page; 2014 opening from Wikipedia (ZHdK moved in autumn 2014). The internal ramp is from general knowledge of the building, not from these sources; trim it from the line if in doubt.

name: German Maritime Museum (Scharoun building)
features: Scharoun's last building: ship-like white volumes stepping along the harbour, with a museum fleet moored outside.
note: Wikipedia: building 'planned by Hans Scharoun', opened 5 September 1975 (Scharoun died in 1972, so it was completed after his death). The 2000s extension by Dietrich Bangert is a separate building; the photos chosen show the Scharoun building. 'Last building' is general knowledge; check.

name: Berlin Musical Instrument Museum
by: Edgar Wisniewski, after designs by Hans Scharoun
features: Scharoun's open, terraced museum landscape of stairs and galleries, beside his Philharmonie at the Kulturforum.
note: Wikipedia: building constructed 1979-1984 by Edgar Wisniewski after designs by Hans Scharoun; shared with the State Institute for Music Research. Interiors (File:Berlin Musikinstrumentenmuseum 2.jpg, 3.jpg, CC BY 3.0) show the terraced hall well.

name: Kanzlerbungalow
features: Flat-roofed glass pavilion for West Germany's chancellors: two square courtyard wings set low in a park.
note: No English article of its own. Wikipedia: by Sep Ruf, the chancellor's residence 1964-1999. 1964 is the year it came into use; the aerial photo (Kanzlerbungalow2.jpg) shows the two square courtyard wings. Photos are in year subcategories (in 2009, 2010, 2012).

name: Plenary Building of the Bundestag, Bonn
features: Glass parliament for democracy on view: transparent walls, a light steel roof and a sunken round chamber by the Rhine.
note: Wikipedia (Behnisch): 'Plenary Complex of the German Parliament', 1987-92, Bonn; competition won in 1973. Used by the Bundestag only until 1999; now part of the World Conference Center Bonn. The sunken round chamber is from general knowledge; the interior photos are in Category:Interior of Plenargebäude (Bundeshaus, Bonn).

name: Kunstmuseum Basel, New Building
features: Angular block faced in grey concrete bricks, kept to the old museum's height; a lettering frieze is set into the wall.
note: Wikipedia: 'an angled building, faced with concrete bricks', same height as the original museum, completed April 2016, by Christ & Gantenbein after a competition.

name: Schaulager
features: Art warehouse walled in concrete mixed with gravel from the site; a white funnel-shaped forecourt cuts in.

photos.file: File:Entree of the Schaulager museum, Münchenstein, 2018.jpg

note: Wikipedia: built 2002/2003 for the Laurenz Foundation, designed by Herzog & de Meuron, opened 2003, 'an open warehouse' for storing art. The excavated-gravel walls are general knowledge, not in the article; trim if in doubt.

name: New Monte Rosa Hut
features: Five-storey polygonal mountain hut in an aluminium shell, with a spiral timber interior, nearly energy self-sufficient.

photos.file: File:Neue Monte Rosa Hütte in summer 2016 front.jpg
File:New Monte Rosa Hut in Monte Rosa massif.jpeg

note: Wikipedia: designed by Andrea Deplazes of ETH Zurich, inaugurated 2009 at 2,883 m above the Grenzgletscher; prefabricated, flown up in 3,000 helicopter trips. Interior photo: File:Neue Monte Rosa Huette4.JPG (CC BY-SA 3.0). City is the nearest town; the hut is on the Monte Rosa massif.

name: Deutsches Architekturmuseum (DAM)
features: A 19th-century villa gutted and rebuilt inside as a 'house within a house': a gridded white shell rising through it.
note: Wikipedia: housed in an 18th/19th-century villa; Ungers redesigned the interior (1979-1984) as 'elemental Platonic buildings within elemental Platonic buildings'. Interior views DAM 02.jpg and DAM 13.jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0) show the house-within-a-house well; the lead photo shows the street front with Ungers' red sandstone arcade.

name: Museum Brandhorst
features: Facade of 36,000 vertical ceramic louvres in 23 coloured glazes that blend into one shimmering surface from afar.
note: Wikipedia: opened 21 May 2009; 36,000 vertical ceramic louvres in 23 glazes. Facade close-up: File:Museum Brandhorst Fassadendetail 2.jpg (CC BY 3.0).

name: GSW Headquarters
features: Thin curved slab added to a 1950s tower; its west double facade of pink and orange shading panels ventilates it.
note: Wikipedia lists 'GSW Headquarters', Berlin, 1999; Commons file descriptions give 82 m height and a double glass facade. Natural ventilation through the double facade is general knowledge of the building; check before publishing.

name: German Environment Agency (Umweltbundesamt), Dessau
features: Long curving office ring in timber and coloured glass bands around a glazed atrium, on a former rail-works site.
note: Wikipedia lists 'Federal Environmental Agency', Dessau, 2005. The ring plan, atrium and rail-works site are general knowledge, consistent with the photos (old brick station buildings beside it); check before publishing.

name: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm Centre
features: University library behind a rigid grid of narrow stone piers; inside, reading terraces step around a top-lit hall.
note: Humboldt University's central library. Wikipedia (Max Dudler) lists it 2009. Reading-room photos: File:Grimm-Zentrum-Lesesaal.jpg and File:Jacob-und-Wilhelm-Grimm-Zentrum-005.JPG (CC BY-SA 3.0) show the terraced hall.

name: Tour Total (Jean-Monnet-Tower)
features: 69 m office tower wrapped in a grid of faceted precast-concrete fins that shift with the light.
note: No English Wikipedia article (en 'Tour Total' is the Paris tower). Architect, 2012 opening and 69 m height from the Commons category's Wikidata infobox. Faceted precast fins: general knowledge, visible in File:Berlin moabit tour total 19.01.2013 12-57-46 ShiftN.jpg; check. Now branded TotalEnergies.

name: Tegel Airport, Terminal A
features: Hexagonal ring terminal around an open square of car parks and taxis, famous for its very short walks to the gates.
note: Wikipedia: hexagon-shaped ring terminal with parking in the middle, inaugurated November 1974; designs by 'Gerkan, Marg und Partner' (cited in a reference). Airport closed in 2020; the terminal is being converted for Berlin TXL / Urban Tech Republic. The category is large (planes, history); an aerial of the hexagon would be a better lead if one is found.

name: Stuttgart City Library (Stadtbibliothek am Mailänder Platz)
features: Plain cube on a 9x9 facade grid; inside, a silent 'heart' room and a white funnel-shaped hall rising to a skylight.
note: Wikipedia: international competition won by Eun Young Yi; built 2010 to 24 October 2011; cube with nine floors above ground; facade of 9x9 glass blocks; central 'heart'; funnel-shaped hall from the fifth level. The skylight is general knowledge; check. Architect is Korean-born, based in Cologne.

name: Paul Löbe House
features: Parliament offices on the 'Band des Bundes': a glass end hall under a thin flat roof, bridged across the Spree.

photos.file: File:141019 Sprung über die Spree und Paul-Löbe-Haus.jpg

note: Wikipedia: Stephan Braunfels won the competition for both the Paul Löbe and Marie-Elisabeth Lüders Houses; built 1997-2002; opened 2001 (the infobox gives 2002 completion); part of Schultes and Frank's 'Band des Bundes'; central hall through the whole building; bridges to the Lüders House over the Spree.

name: Kranhäuser (Crane Houses)
by: Alfons Linster and Hadi Teherani (BRT Architekten)
features: Three 17-storey upside-down L blocks on the Rhine, cantilevered like the harbour cranes they recall.
note: Wikipedia: three 17-storey buildings, upside-down L like harbour cranes, about 62 m high and 70 m long; by Alfons Linster and Hadi Teherani of BRT; construction began 2006, first completed 2008 (the set finished later). Two offices and one housing block.

name: Neuer Zollhof
features: Three leaning, curving office blocks in white plaster, stainless steel and red brick on Düsseldorf's old harbour.

photos.file: File:2015.09.26.162620 Gehry Buildings Neuer Zollhof Düsseldorf.jpg

note: Wikipedia: three buildings by Frank Gehry, completed 1998; tallest 14 storeys, just under 50 m; white plaster, stainless steel and red brick claddings.

name: Museum der bildenden Künste, Leipzig
by: Hufnagel Pütz Rafaelian (Karl Hufnagel, Peter Pütz, Michael Rafaelian)
features: Glass-clad box on a former city square, framed by lower corner buildings that rebuild the old street block.

photos.file: File:Leipzig - Katharinenstraße - 10Museum der bildenden Künste 01 ies.jpg
File:Leipzig - Museum der bildenden Künste Leipzig.jpg

note: Wikipedia: Hufnagel Pütz Rafaelian won the 1997 competition; opened 4 December 2004 on the former Sachsenplatz; 'a compact building mass framed by angled structures in the corners of the pre-war street block'. The glass cladding is visible in the photos, not stated in the article. Inner court: File:Leipzig - Museum der bildenden Künste Leipzig (1).jpg (CC BY 2.0).

name: Ohel Jakob Synagogue
by: Wandel Hoefer Lorch (Rena Wandel-Hoefer, Wolfgang Lorch)
features: Rough travertine base like the Western Wall, topped by a glass cube in a bronze star-of-David lattice: the tent.

photos.file: File:Blick auf den St.-Jakobs-Platz und die Hauptsynagoge in München.JPG

note: Wikipedia: architects Rena Wandel-Hoefer and Wolfgang Lorch; built 2004-2006, inaugurated 9 November 2006; part of the Jewish Center with the museum and community centre. The Western Wall and tent readings and the lattice pattern are general knowledge, not in the article; check. Photos are in the Jewish Centre category (synagogue, museum and community centre together); interiors in Category:Interior of the Hauptsynagoge Ohel Jakob (Munich).

name: Kant-Dreieck
features: Gridded office tower on a triangular plot, crowned by a huge sheet-metal 'sail' that turns in the wind.
note: No English Wikipedia article. Architect from the Commons category's Wikidata infobox; 1994 and the movable riveted sheet-metal sail from Commons file descriptions. Check the year against another source before publishing.

name: Züblin-Haus
features: Two office slabs facing across a huge glass-roofed hall, with free-standing stair towers and bridges inside.

photos.file: File:Verwaltungsgebäude der Ed. Züblin AG, Albstadtweg 3, Stuttgart-Möhringen.jpg

note: Headquarters of the construction firm Ed. Züblin AG. No English Wikipedia article. Architects from the Commons category's Wikidata infobox; the category files it under 'Built in 1985' while two photo titles say 1984. Interior hall photos are in the same category.

name: Norddeutsche Landesbank (NORD/LB) Headquarters
features: Glass perimeter block around a planted court, with a tower of glass boxes stacked and twisted off a central core.

photos.file: File:Nord LB administration building Hanover Germany.jpg
File:Inner yard Nord-LB office building Hanover Germany.jpg

note: Wikipedia (Günter Behnisch): 'North German State Clearing Bank', 1998-2002, Hanover. Commons credits 'Behnisch Architekten'; the firm at the time was Behnisch, Behnisch & Partner (Stefan Behnisch). A Commons photo shows roof mirrors that direct daylight into the court.

name: Academy of Arts, Pariser Platz
by: Günter Behnisch with Werner Durth (Behnisch & Partner)
features: An all-glass front on Pariser Platz, defying the square's stone rules, opening onto the old academy halls behind.
commons_category: Category:Akademie der Künste Berlin (Pariser Platz building)
note: Wikipedia (Günter Behnisch): 'Academy of Arts Building', 1993-2005, a glass building beside the reconstructed Hotel Adlon. Co-design by Werner Durth and the fight over Pariser Platz's stone-facade rules are general knowledge; check before publishing.

name: BMW Headquarters (BMW Tower) and BMW Museum
features: Four linked cylinders like an engine, hung from a central support tower; beside it, the museum's round 'cylinder head'.

photos.file: File:BMW Welt and BMW Headquarters, Munich, Germany.jpg

note: Wikipedia: by Austrian architect Karl Schwanzer, both tower and museum; built 1968-1972, opened 1973; 101 m; the cylinders are suspended on a central support tower and floors were assembled on the ground then lifted. Treated as one entry with the museum beside it (museum established 1973, renovated 2004-2008).

name: Swiss Embassy, Berlin (extension)
features: A sheer concrete block butted against the surviving 1870s embassy palace, the last old building in its district.
note: Wikipedia (Diener & Diener): 'Swiss Embassy Berlin', 1995-2000. The old palace dates from the 1870s (a Commons file is titled 'Berlin Schweizer Botschaft 1863', so check the date) and was the only building left standing around it after the war; general knowledge, check. The extension's east wall carries an artwork by Helmut Federle (not in sources here).

name: Axel Springer Campus
features: Dark glass office cube split by a diagonal valley of terraced open-plan floors, seen through a faceted glass wall.
note: Wikipedia: Axel Springer Campus, Berlin (2020), a cube-shaped office building by Rem Koolhaas and OMA. The terraced diagonal 'valley' inside is general knowledge, visible through the faceted glass in the photos; check.

name: Berlin Hauptbahnhof
by: Meinhard von Gerkan (gmp, von Gerkan, Marg and Partners)
features: Crossing station: an east-west glass train shed over a north-south line below, straddled by two office bridges.
note: Wikipedia infobox: architect Meinhard von Gerkan of Gerkan, Marg and Partners; opened 26 May 2006. The two-level crossing and the office 'bridge' buildings are general knowledge, visible in the photos; check wording. Engineers: Schlaich Bergermann (not in sources here).

name: ADAC Headquarters
features: 93 m tower rising from a long, curving base; its glass skin in 22 shades of yellow and blue reads as one colour field.
note: Wikipedia: built 2006-2011, opened 22 March 2012, 93 m and 23 floors; architect Sauerbruch Hutton, structural engineer Werner Sobek. Year given as 2011 completion (Sauerbruch Hutton's list says 2012). The '22 shades' figure is general knowledge, not checked; trim to 'yellow and blue shades' if in doubt.

name: Kunstmuseum Bonn
features: Pale concrete galleries under a vast thin roof on slender columns, shading a forecourt shared with the Kunsthalle.
note: Wikipedia: by BJSS (Axel Schultes) and Jürgen Pleuser, opened 1992; three entrances. The canopy-on-columns description is from the photos and general knowledge. Do not use File:Bonn Kunstmuseum by Niederkasseler - panoramio.jpg: it shows the Bundeskunsthalle's cones. Schultes later designed the Federal Chancellery (already on the wall).

name: Marco Polo Tower
features: 55 m apartment tower whose floor plates twist from storey to storey, so deep balconies shade the glass below.
note: Wikipedia lists 'Marco-Polo-Tower, Hamburg, Germany 2010' among Behnisch Architekten's projects; Commons infobox gives 55 m and inception August 2009. Stands next to Behnisch's Unilever-Haus (already on the wall). The rotating floor plates are visible in the photos; the shading purpose is general knowledge.

name: Library and Learning Center, Vienna University of Economics
features: Leaning, striated block whose dark glazed reading room cantilevers far over the campus square.
commons_category: Category:WU Wien, Library and Learning Center

photos.file: File:Campus WU LC D1 TC DSC 1440w.jpg
File:WU Wien, Library & Learning Center, Zaha Hadid 001.JPG

note: Wikipedia (Zaha Hadid) dates it 2013, when the new WU campus opened; other articles give 2008, the competition year. Centrepiece of the WU campus, whose other buildings are by BUSarchitektur, CRAB, Estudio Carme Pinós, Atelier Hitoshi Abe and NO.MAD (general knowledge).

name: Gasometer B, Vienna
features: An 1890s brick gasholder turned into flats, with a bent, shield-like slab of new apartments leaning against it.
note: Wikipedia: gasholders built 1896-1899; four converted 1999-2001 by Jean Nouvel (A), Coop Himmelblau (B), Manfred Wehdorn (C) and Wilhelm Holzbauer (D); opened 30 October 2001. This entry is Gasometer B only; the 'shield' name is general knowledge, not in the article.

name: Zentralsparkasse Branch, Favoritenstrasse
features: Bank front of bulging, rippling steel panels between plain houses; inside, a giant concrete hand holds the stair.
note: Wikipedia (Domenig): 'Zentralsparkasse bank, Vienna' 1974-79 and an Austrian builders prize for the Z-branch Favoriten in 1981; Commons gives 1975-79. The concrete hand is visible in File:Zentralsparkassenfiliale-Favoritenstraße-(Günther-Domenig,-1975–79)-(3).jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0). Now known as the Domenig-Haus; no longer a bank.

name: Loisium Wine World
features: An aluminium-clad cube among the vineyards, cut by narrow slots, that leads down into old wine cellars.
note: No English Wikipedia article; Steven Holl's article does not mention it. Architect from the Commons category's Wikidata infobox; 2003 from its 'Built in Lower Austria in 2003' category. The link to the cellars and the cut-slot pattern are general knowledge plus the photos; check. Holl also built the Loisium hotel next to it (not included).

name: Kaufhaus Tyrol
features: Department store front broken into a gently angled row of stone-framed bays that keeps the rhythm of the old street.
note: No English Wikipedia article. Architects and opening date (4 March 2010) from the Commons category's Wikidata infobox. Type set to Workplace for lack of a retail type in the vocabulary. The stone-framed bays are from the photos.

name: Lentos Art Museum
features: 130 m glass-skinned box on the Danube that glows in changing colours at night, with a large opening to the river.
note: Wikipedia: by Zurich firm Weber & Hofer, opened May 2003, 130 m long, about 8,000 m2, transparent glass facade lit at night, on the Danube. The river-facing opening is visible in the photos (not described in the article); trim if in doubt.

name: Wiener Stadthalle
features: Postwar arena whose big hall hangs its roof over a row of raking concrete struts along a glazed foyer.
note: Wikipedia: Roland Rainer designed the original halls, built 1953-1958; Halls A and B opened 19 October 1957, Hall D 21 June 1958; later halls E (1994) and F (2006) by others. The raking struts and roof are described from the photos; check.

name: Murinsel
features: A floating steel-and-glass shell in the river Mur, a café and amphitheatre linked to both banks by footbridges.
note: Wikipedia: an artificial floating island in the Mur linking both banks, designed by New York artist Vito Acconci for Graz's year as 2003 European Capital of Culture. The café and amphitheatre programme is general knowledge; check.

name: Werkraum Haus
features: Showroom for the Bregenzerwald craftsmen's guild: one big dark roof floating over an all-glass hall.

photos.file: File:Werkraum Haus von Peter Zumthor in Andelsbuch 1.JPG
File:Werkraum Haus von Peter Zumthor in Andelsbuch 4.jpg
File:Werkraum Haus von Peter Zumthor in Andelsbuch 3.jpg

note: Architect from Commons file titles; 2013 from the category 'Built in Vorarlberg in 2013'. Werkraum Bregenzerwald is the craftsmen's association (founded 1999). The roof's timber structure is general knowledge; the photos show a dark roof edge and glass walls.

name: LifeCycle Tower One (LCT ONE)
features: Eight-storey prototype of a prefabricated timber-hybrid office system, its timber slabs set floor by floor.
note: No English Wikipedia article. From the Commons category: architect Hermann Kaufmann, inception 2011, 27 m, eight-storey timber hybrid; the system is meant to reach up to 100 m / 30 storeys; a file shows the finished shell in 2012. 'Set floor by floor' is general knowledge of its prefabricated assembly; check. The facade is clad, so the timber is not visible in the photos.

name: 2226 Office Building
features: Thick-walled white cube with deep, tall window reveals, built to stay comfortable without heating or cooling plant.

photos.file: File:Bürogebäude 2226 Lustenau Österreich 2013 Baumschlager Eberle Architekten.jpg

note: No English Wikipedia article. Architect and 2013 from Commons file titles and categories. The 'no heating, cooling or mechanical ventilation' concept (the name refers to 22-26 degrees C) and the thick brick walls are general knowledge, not in the sources reached; check before publishing. The photos look like professional press images uploaded under free licences; worth a glance at the licence pages.

name: Fiore di pietra
features: Summit restaurant whose stone-clad walls fold outward like petals around a glazed core, on the cliff edge.

photos.file: File:Botta Fiore die Petra Monte Genoroso.jpg

note: Wikipedia: restaurant by Mario Botta, inaugurated 29 March 2017 on Monte Generoso (on the Swiss-Italian border, reached by rack railway). The petal-like stone walls are described from the photos. City field holds the mountain; the nearest municipality is Rovio/Mendrisio.

name: Bagno Pubblico, Bellinzona
by: Aurelio Galfetti, Flora Ruchat-Roncati and Ivo Trümpy
features: Public pools strung under a long raised concrete walkway that runs from the town to the river across the valley.
note: Wikipedia (Galfetti): 'Städtisches Freibad, 1967-70, Bellinzona'; Commons infobox: Galfetti, Ruchat-Roncati and Trümpy, built to 1970, Swiss cultural property of national significance (class A). The photos show the pools and gardens but none shows the raised walkway well (it appears at the edge of III); a better photo of the passerella would help. The walkway-to-the-river idea is general knowledge.

name: Palestra (Gymnasium), Losone
features: A sports hall wrapped in a dense ring of tall concrete piers that carry the roof and filter the light.
note: Wikipedia (Vacchini) shows the 'Palestra Caserma' in Losone without a date; the Commons file gives 'Palestra 1995-1997 (competition 1990)'. Only two usable photos; the lead (2048 px) is a distant frontal view. The piers-carry-the-roof reading is general knowledge; check.
